issues.body: join_eq_r_repeated_pair_pads_and_accepts calls two_pair_universe(), which commits A rows with join keys JK and JK2 and matching B rows with both keys. The true join cardinality at slots A[2] x B[0] is therefore 2, not 1 as the test commentary states. Repeating the first pair does test lane reuse, but this fixture does not validate the specifically claimed case that an actual one-match graph can fill R=2 lanes. On this honesty-sensitive surface, the test description and exercised invariant must agree.
issues.fix_hint: Build JR2 from committed graphs containing exactly one genuine joined pair (or a second nonmatching row if multi-row coverage is desired), assert/use those commitments, and repeat that sole pair across both lanes. Keep JR1 on two_pair_universe() for the distinct-pair case.
issues.title: JR2 claims N=1 but constructs a two-match graph

verdict.summary: Round 2's major cardinality overclaim is materially fixed: the revised code and documentation consistently state that R lanes may repeat, prove only existence of a genuine match in cardinality terms, and establish no bound on the true join cardinality N. The per-lane relation and adversarial tests otherwise support the scoped circuit statement. One test remains internally false, however: JR2 says its universe has N=1 and presents itself as the one-match padding witness, but it calls two_pair_universe(), whose committed graphs have two genuine joined pairs. Thus the test does not exercise the exact scenario its comments claim. This is a new, lower-severity finding, so progress is regressing under the mandated scale.
